# Why the per-entry horizon is safe

Written for: contributors who change how a replicated space collects tombstones, renews leases or judges a re-offered copy, and reviewers of that work.

A replica keeps a *tombstone* for an entry that left the space, so that an old copy of the entry arriving late is recognised and not taken back.
Until now a withdrawn entry's tombstone stayed `L + 2 x maxLease`, where `L` is the entry's last lease expiry.
Under the hint `wire.horizon=1` from every member in view, a withdrawn entry whose writer the replica can vouch for becomes collectable at `L + max(5 min, MAX_DRIFT)` instead, ten minutes past L with the drift ceiling of SPEC §11 (SPEC §7.3).
Under either rule a withdrawn entry is never collectable before `L + MAX_DRIFT`, the drift floor of owner decision 22 (2026-11-15).
This note says why that is safe, and when it stops being safe.
The model and the checks behind it are in this folder and in `agentspaces-space`.

## The words

- **Lease register.** Each entry carries one lease: an expiry and the stamp of the write that set it. Two copies merge by keeping the lease with the higher stamp.
- **L.** The expiry the issuer's replica holds at the moment it cancels the entry. The cancel writes no new lease, so the withdrawn state carries L.
- **Copy.** Any state of the entry anywhere: held by a replica, or travelling in a message, however old.
- **Present and unexpired.** Neither withdrawn nor completed, and the lease expiry is later than the replica's own clock. A reader can see it and a taker can take it.
- **Sweep.** The pass that collects (drops) a state once its horizon has passed on the replica's clock.
- **Door.** The check every incoming copy meets. A copy whose own horizon has passed on the replica's clock is refused (SPEC §7.3, a MUST).
- **Horizons.** Lapsed (present, lease run out): `expiry + min(2 x maxLease, 5 min)`. Completed: `expiry + 2 x maxLease`. Withdrawn: `L + max(2 x maxLease, MAX_DRIFT)` under the legacy rule, and `L + max(5 min, MAX_DRIFT)` per entry.
- **MAX_DRIFT.** The clock drift ceiling of SPEC §11, ten minutes: any two conforming clocks differ by at most this much.

## The claim

Two statements. Under the assumptions below, both hold in every run.

1. **No resurrection.** A replica that has held the entry withdrawn never again holds it present and unexpired by its own clock.
2. **The door refuses re-offers.** After a replica collects a state, every copy that the state already covers is refused at that replica's door. A copy is covered when merging it would change nothing.

## The assumptions

- **A1. Only the issuer writes the lease register.** A write and a renewal write it. A cancel and a completion do not. A take's lease is a separate claim and never touches the register.
- **A2. A renewal never shortens.** The new expiry is `max(current, now + extension)`, and a renewal needs the entry present and unexpired on the renewing replica (SPEC §7.2, v0.1.35).
- **A3. One node renews per identity.** All of the issuer's lease writes happen on one replica, one after another.
- **A4. Clocks never run backwards.** On each replica, the sweep and the door read the same local clock.
- **A5. The door applies the same rule as the sweep.**
- **A6. The withdrawn horizon is never shorter than the lapse horizon.** `max(5 min, MAX_DRIFT) >= min(2 x maxLease, 5 min)` always holds.
- **A7. One write per entry id.** Entry ids are issuer-generated UUIDs, so no second write adds a fresh copy of the same id.

## The argument

**Step 1. The issuer's last lease is the largest.**
- By A1 and A3, every lease write happens on one replica, in order, each with a higher stamp than the one before.
- By A2, each write's expiry is at least the previous one's.
- So the lease with the highest stamp also has the largest expiry.

**Step 2. Every copy has expiry at most L.**
- The cancel happens on the issuer's replica after all of its renewals.
- After the cancel no renewal can follow, since a renewal needs the entry present (A2).
- So the cancel carries the newest lease, and L is the largest expiry any copy of the entry ever carried.
- A merge only ever keeps one of the leases it was given.
- So no copy, held or in flight, old or new, has an expiry past L. The model calls this `LeaseBound`.

**Step 3. While a replica holds the tombstone, nothing revives it.**
- Withdrawal and completion are monotone in the merge.
- By A7 no new copy of the entry can be added.
- So a replica holding the withdrawn state never turns it present again.

**Step 4. After collection, the door refuses every older copy.**
- A replica R collects the tombstone at a clock reading `t >= L + max(5 min, MAX_DRIFT)`, so `t >= L + 5 min`.
- By A4, every later reading on R is at least t.
- Now take any copy offered to R later:
  - A present copy has expiry `e <= L` (step 2). On R's clock it lapsed at e, and its lapse horizon `e + min(2 x maxLease, 5 min) <= L + 5 min <= t` has passed (A6). The door refuses it (A5).
  - A withdrawn copy carries the same L. Its horizon, the same as the collected state's, has passed, so the door refuses it.
  - A completed copy may pass the door, since completions keep a longer horizon. A completed copy is not present, so it cannot make the entry present.
- So R never holds the entry present and unexpired again.

**There is no delay bound in this argument.**
- The legacy horizon assumed that every lagging copy arrives within two lease periods.
- Here nothing is assumed about when a copy arrives: a copy arriving a year late is refused by the same arithmetic.
- Collection and the door read one clock, so clock skew between replicas does not enter the claim, which is about a replica that held the withdrawal.
- Skew does matter to a replica that never heard of the withdrawal. The drift floor covers it; see [A trailing clock, and the drift floor](#a-trailing-clock-and-the-drift-floor).

## What breaks it

Each break below violates an assumption.
The Java model check finds each one; the traces are printed by `HorizonModelCheckTest`.

- **One identity renews from two nodes (A3).** Node a cancels with `L = 1`. Node b, holding the same identity and an older copy, renews it to `e = 3`, and a never hears of it. Node a collects at `L + grace = 2`, and b's copy then passes a's door as present and unexpired. The model finds this in 12 steps. `HorizonSimulationTest.aSecondNodeRenewingTheSameIdentityBreaksTheHorizon` shows the same on the real classes.
- **A writer that shortens (A2).** The issuer writes with `e = 3`, a copy leaves, the issuer shortens to `e = 1` and cancels. The issuer collects at 2 and takes the old copy back. The model finds this in 12 steps. A member that predates SPEC v0.1.35, such as one of release 0.6.0, renews as `now + extension` and can shorten.
- **A restart that loses the issuer's register** and renews again from a fresh replica is the two-node case.
- **A rule mistake (A5, A6).** A door that judges by a different rule than the sweep, or a withdrawn horizon shorter than the lapse horizon, lets a present copy through.

## Why `wire.horizon=1` from every member in view

- The hint is a member's promise to keep A2 and A3: it renews by the max rule, renews only its own present and unexpired entries, and renews from one node per identity.
- The precondition has two halves. A replica checks both before it uses the shorter horizon on a withdrawal.
  - **The view's half.** Every member in view advertises the hint. Every member can be an issuer, and an unhinted member's copies travel through every other member, so one unhinted member in view is enough to break step 1 for its own entries. The rule disengages at once when one joins. It engages again only after three fully hinted rounds, so a member that flaps cannot make it thrash.
  - **The writer's half.** The node that wrote the entry (the replica of its add dot) is this replica, or a hinted member that has been in this replica's view for one maxLease plus five minutes. A withdrawal by any other writer keeps the later of the two horizons here, `L + max(2 x maxLease, MAX_DRIFT)`. With the drift floor under both, the legacy horizon is never the shorter one; the later of the two is kept anyway, so that a writer leaving the view never brings a withdrawal's horizon closer whatever the two rules become. (Before the floor, the legacy horizon was the shorter one when maxLease was under 2.5 minutes.)
- **Why the view alone is not enough** (found by the adversarial review of step 5b). A replica's view says nothing about writers outside it.
  - A partition can leave a hinted replica alone, or with hinted members only, while an unhinted writer works on the other side.
  - That writer can write, renew from a second node or shorten, and cancel, out of sight. Then it can leave before the partition heals.
  - The replica receives the withdrawal, and later the long copy. Judged by its view alone, it would collect the withdrawal at the per-entry horizon and take the copy back present.
  - `AdversaryHorizonViewScopeTest` replays this. Two writers share one identity and keep the legacy setting, as the precondition tells them to. The judge's view is empty. Before the fix, the judge took the copy back under the per-entry rule. Now the writer is out of view, so the judge keeps the withdrawal under both settings.
- **Why the writer must have been in view a while.** A writer that has just come into view may have renewed out of sight before. Every copy it renewed then lapses within one maxLease of its arrival, and passes its own lapse horizon five minutes later. After that the door refuses those copies, so the writer can be trusted.
- **Why the mode also waits after it engages (the settle).** A member can stay in view while its card loses and regains the hint, for example a node that restarts on a newer release under the same peer id. The disengage resets the mode. The settle of one maxLease plus five minutes then lets everything it renewed while unhinted lapse first.
- **What the two waits do not cover.**
  - Both reckon with this replica's own observed maxLease. A writer's lease longer than any this replica has seen is not covered.
  - A node that ran an older release out of this replica's sight, renewed shorter there, then comes into view hinted under the same peer id and waits out its settle, is trusted by then. Its shortened copies are covered only if the shortened-away lease was within this replica's maxLease.
  - Nothing on the wire tells two nodes renewing one identity apart from one. That stays a documented precondition (P40).
- **Two replicas in different modes** need no agreement. Each judges by its own view, its own writers and its own clock. A legacy replica keeps withdrawals at least as long, since both rules keep at least MAX_DRIFT, and longer when its maxLease is over five minutes, since `2 x maxLease` is then over ten. Step 4 allows either (A6 holds either way).

## A trailing clock, and the drift floor

- The claim is about a replica that held the withdrawal. A replica that never heard of it is not covered by steps 1 to 4, and clock drift matters there.
- **The window, before the floor.** Say every replica that held the withdrawal collects it at its own `L + 5 min`. A replica Y never got the withdrawal, and its clock trails by 8 minutes, within `MAX_DRIFT` (10 minutes, SPEC §11). A third replica that also never got it hands Y an old present copy, with `e <= L`. On Y's clock the copy is still unexpired, so Y shows the cancelled entry live, for up to `MAX_DRIFT - 5 min = 5 min`, with no tombstone left anywhere to correct it.
- **The legacy rule had the same window** when `2 x maxLease < MAX_DRIFT`, that is, when maxLease was under five minutes.
- **The floor (owner decision 22, 2026-11-15).** A withdrawn entry is never collectable before `L + MAX_DRIFT`, under either rule. So the per-entry horizon is `L + max(5 min, MAX_DRIFT)`, and the legacy one `L + max(2 x maxLease, MAX_DRIFT)`.
- **Why it closes the window.**
  - The first replica to collect does so at a clock reading `t >= L + MAX_DRIFT`.
  - Every other replica's clock is within `MAX_DRIFT` of that one, so it reads at least `t - MAX_DRIFT >= L`, and clocks never run backwards (A4).
  - Every copy has `e <= L` (step 2, for writers that keep A2 and A3).
  - So from the first collection on, no copy is unexpired on any replica's clock, and no replica can turn the entry live, whether or not it ever heard of the withdrawal.
- **Lapsed entries keep their grace.** A lapse is judged from the lease register every replica holds alike. An entry still unexpired on a trailing clock is live there by the same rule as everywhere, so no tombstone is needed to correct it.
- **The cost.** A withdrawal's tombstone lives five minutes longer under the per-entry rule (ten minutes instead of five), and under the legacy rule up to ten minutes instead of `2 x maxLease` when maxLease is under five minutes. Spaces with longer leases see no change under the legacy rule.
- **The model shows both.** `NoLateLive` is a step property: once some replica has collected a withdrawal, no step turns any replica live. With the floor it holds in every configuration, `HorizonPerEntryDrift.cfg` (drift twice the grace) and `HorizonPerEntryLegacyDrift.cfg` (legacy, two leases under the drift) included. Without it (`HorizonPerEntryDriftNoFloor.cfg`, `HorizonPerEntryLegacyDriftNoFloor.cfg`) `NoLateLive` breaks: in the per-entry case, the issuer writes with expiry 1, sends a copy to replica 2, cancels and collects at its clock 2, and the copy reaches replica 2 at clock 0.

## Why completed entries keep 2 x maxLease

- **The completer is not the issuer.** A completed state carries the completer's view of the lease, which may be older than the issuer's newest renewal.
  - The issuer may renew while the entry is taken.
  - The issuer may not yet have heard of the take at all.
- **So step 1 says nothing about a completion.** Its expiry is not the largest any copy carries.
- **What protects a completion is delivery.** The legacy window of `2 x maxLease` assumes the completion reaches the issuer, which then stops renewing, and that lagging copies arrive within that window. This is a timing assumption, not a proof.
- **The model shows the assumption failing, under the legacy rule itself.**
  - Replica 2 completes an old copy.
  - The issuer, cut off from it, keeps renewing.
  - Replica 2 collects the completion at `2 x maxLease`.
  - When the cut heals, replica 2 takes the issuer's live copy back. The run is `HorizonModelCheckTest.aCompletionsHorizonRestsOnDeliveryNotOnTheLease`.
  - This behaviour predates the horizon, and the horizon does not change it.
- **The real classes show it too.** In the engaged simulation, where completions are collected at five minutes (harsher than the rule), it happened once in 200 seeds in the recorded run, and twice in an earlier run of the same seeds.
- **A state that is both withdrawn and completed** takes the completed horizon. If it took the shorter one, its completed copies, which carry the older lease, would pass the door again. Those copies are harmless, since they are not present, but every one of them would come back.
- **It keeps the drift floor too** (2026-11-15). Without it, under a maximum lease shorter than half the drift, such a tombstone collected at `L + 2 x maxLease` would let a copy that is withdrawn alone, which keeps `L + MAX_DRIFT`, back through the door. The model found this as soon as the floor was in: `RefusedAtEveryDoor` broke in `HorizonPerEntryLegacyDrift.cfg` at depth 12, where replica 2 completed, then merged the issuer's withdrawal and collected the joint state at `L + 2`. Its horizon is now `L + max(2 x maxLease, MAX_DRIFT)` under both rules.

## How it was checked

**1. An exhaustive explicit-state check in Java** (`agentspaces-space`, `HorizonModelCheckTest`).
- It is the same model as `HorizonPerEntry.tla`, searched breadth-first, with every invariant checked in every reachable state.
- Time is in abstract units, with grace 1 standing for the five minutes. The argument only needs A6.
- `theModelsLegacyRuleIsTheRealOne` ties the model's two rules to `SpaceStateCrdt.collectionHorizon` at the real five minutes and the real ten-minute drift, for lapsed, withdrawn, completed, and withdrawn-and-completed states.
- The drift floor is a constant `DRIFT_FLOOR` of the model and a field of the Java `Config`. Every run has it on except the two that show what it is for.

| Run | Constants (time, drift, lease, grace, stamps, in flight) | States | Transitions | Depth | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Per entry | 4, 1, 3, 1, 3, 1 | 2,476,355 | 11,957,352 | 42 | all hold |
| Per entry, two in flight | 3, 1, 2, 1, 3, 2 | 4,133,764 | 27,346,680 | 36 | all hold |
| Legacy | 4, 1, 3, 1, 3, 1 | 2,300,654 | 11,120,895 | 42 | all hold |
| Drift twice the grace, with the floor | 4, 2, 3, 1, 3, 1 | 4,937,990 | 25,818,664 | 42 | all hold |
| Drift twice the grace, without the floor | 4, 2, 3, 1, 3, 1 | 5,176,065 | 27,035,631 | 42 | the three invariants hold |
| Drift twice the grace, without the floor, `NoLateLive` | 4, 2, 3, 1, 3, 1 | 4,050 when found | 10,666 | 7 | `NoLateLive` broken (the window the floor closes) |
| Legacy, two leases under the drift, with the floor | 4, 3, 1, 1, 3, 1 | 403,456 | 2,136,631 | 35 | all hold |
| Legacy, two leases under the drift, without the floor, `NoLateLive` | 4, 3, 1, 1, 3, 1 | 2,141 when found | 6,182 | 8 | `NoLateLive` broken (the legacy window) |
| Shortening writer | 4, 1, 3, 1, 3, 1 | 203,791 when found | 782,864 | 12 | NoResurrection broken |
| Two nodes, one identity | 4, 1, 3, 1, 3, 1 | 105,180 when found | 386,450 | 12 | NoResurrection broken |
| Completion, legacy | 5, 1, 2, 1, 6, 1 | 1,907,110 when found | 8,338,355 | 26 | CompletionStaysDone broken |

"All hold" covers `NoResurrection`, `RefusedAtEveryDoor`, `LeaseBound` and the step property `NoLateLive`.

The drift run with the floor is not vacuous either: 30,174 of its states hold a collected withdrawal while a present copy still exists, and its door refused 7,007 such copies.

The per-entry run is not vacuous:
- 73,499 of its states hold a collected withdrawal while a present copy still exists somewhere;
- 16,724 of its transitions are a door refusing such a copy.

The two-in-flight run reaches reordering against a collection:
- An earlier version of it (clock 2, leases up to 3) could not. Any renewal that moved the expiry put it past the last collectable one, so every collected withdrawal carried the first lease. The adversarial review found this.
- The constants now let a renewed entry be withdrawn and collected inside the bound: write with expiry 1, renew to 2, cancel, collect at 3.
- 39,548 of its states hold a renewed withdrawal (stamp above 1) collected by a replica while a copy with an older stamp is in flight to that replica. The test asserts this count is positive. Its door refused 61,781 present copies after a collected withdrawal.

**2. A randomized simulation over the real `SpaceStateCrdt` and `ReplicatedSpace`** (`HorizonSimulationTest`).
- Three replicas sit on a `SimNetwork`.
- Each replica has its own fake clock, skewed within plus or minus 5 minutes, so any two clocks stay within `MAX_DRIFT`; the largest skew seen was 600 s.
- Copies travel by anti-entropy pulls that are delayed up to 40 steps (one in eight up to 120), lost one time in seven, reordered, and cut by a partition. The long delays were added with the drift floor: a present copy now reaches a replica that collected its withdrawal only after a long wait in flight.
- Each replica holds the other two in its view. The views form over the network first, then the network is cut for good, and no node ticks again. So copies travel only by the run's own pulls, and the views never change.
- Since the drift floor the run also checks `NoLateLive` after every step, on every replica, for every entry whose withdrawal some replica has collected.
- The engaged run is seeds 1 to 200, 400 steps each. In a recorded run with the drift floor (2026-11-15) it saw:
  - 406 withdrawals and 156 completions;
  - 1,010 withdrawn tombstones collected, 912 of them under the per-entry rule, 543 of those on a replica other than the writer's;
  - 28 present copies refused at the door after their withdrawal was collected, 23 of them after a per-entry collection (21 to 24 over three runs);
  - 287,046 checks of `NoLateLive`;
  - no violation.
- The shadow run is seeds 1,001 to 1,200, 400 steps each, on the unhinted rule, with one 30-minute lease written first. Since the floor, the run's own leases (at most four minutes) give both rules the same ten minutes for a withdrawal, so the long lease keeps the legacy horizon an hour out. The per-entry rule would have collected 254,619 times. Each time the run checked that every copy anywhere would be refused, 2,092 of them present copies. It found no violation.
- A seed fixes the schedule, but not the keys, which are fresh each run. So the counts move by a few percent from run to run. Before the drift floor (the writer-scope fix of 2026-11-15, delays up to 40 steps) the engaged run saw 866 collections and 27 refusals, 17 of them after a per-entry collection, and the shadow run 16,070 checks with 1,399 present copies. Before the writer-scope fix, with empty views, the engaged run saw 813 collections at `L + 5 min` and 30 refusals.

**3. The TLA+ model** (`HorizonPerEntry.tla`) **has not been model-checked yet.**
- No TLA+ tools were installed, and nothing could be downloaded.


## What the model leaves out

- **One entry and one write.** Entries do not interact in the rule, since each is judged by its own lease.
- **Stamps.** They are a global counter, one total order that respects each node's own order. A real HLC gives one such order.
- **Claims are local flags.** A take's lease never touches the register (A1), so it cannot change any expiry.
- **What a replica sends.** In the model a replica sends its merged state. A real replica forwards the most advanced signed state it holds, which is a state some replica held, so the model can also deliver it late.
- **What the simulation covers instead.** The model has no far-future deferral, no recordless deltas, no shards and no acknowledgements. The simulation on the real classes covers acknowledgements and the real door.
- **Small constants.** Abstract units and small bounds keep the search finite. The argument above does not depend on their size.

## Notes for the implementation of the rule

- **The seam.**
  - `SpaceStateCrdt` gains a second static form that takes the mode.
  - The two existing public forms stay the unhinted rule.
  - `ReplicatedSpace` reads the mode from the view.
  - `HorizonSimulationTest` and `HorizonModelCheckTest` each mark the hook where the real form replaces the modelled one.
  - The engaged simulation's `maxLease` override goes when the mode exists.
- **`L + 5 min` against `L + min(2 x maxLease, 5 min)`.** The design names the first. Both are safe, since step 4 needs only A6. The second is never later than the legacy horizon when leases are short. The choice was for 5b, which took the first (see As built). Owner decision 22 then put the drift floor under both rules, so the per-entry horizon is `L + max(5 min, MAX_DRIFT)`.
- **A finding about the legacy rule.**
  - The unhinted horizon reads the replica's observed maxLease, which grows when a longer lease is seen.
  - So a tombstone collected under a small maxLease is taken back once a larger one has been seen. The shadow simulation saw it 11 times in 200 seeds in the recorded run (between 7 and 10 in earlier ones), each time after such growth.
  - It returns as a tombstone, never present.
  - The per-entry withdrawn horizon does not read maxLease, so withdrawals stop bouncing. Completions and short lapses still do.

## As built (step 5b, 2026-11-15)

- **The rule.** `SpaceStateCrdt.Horizon` is `LEGACY` or `PER_ENTRY`. The new static forms `collectable(state, now, maxLease, horizon)`, `collectionHorizon(state, maxLease, horizon)` and `keepMillis(state, maxLease, horizon)` take it. The old public forms are the `LEGACY` rule, unchanged.
- **`L + max(5 min, MAX_DRIFT)`, fixed.** A withdrawn entry under `PER_ENTRY` keeps the later of `LAPSED_GRACE_MILLIS` and `WITHDRAWN_DRIFT_FLOOR_MILLIS` (`HybridLogicalClock.MAX_DRIFT_MILLIS`, ten minutes) past its own L, whatever the maximum lease. Step 5b built `L + 5 min`; owner decision 22 (2026-11-15) added the floor, in `SpaceStateCrdt.keepMillis`, under both rules. It keeps withdrawals from bouncing when the observed maximum lease grows (the finding above). Under `LEGACY` a withdrawal keeps `max(2 x maxLease, MAX_DRIFT)`, so in a space whose leases are all under five minutes both rules keep ten minutes. That costs a few tombstones, not safety.
- **Completed, and withdrawn-and-completed,** keep `2 x maxLease`.
- **The mode comes from the view.** `GroupRuntime.viewAdvertisesHorizon()` is true when this node and every member in view advertise `wire.horizon=1`. A member whose card has not arrived counts as unhinted.
- **The writer is judged per state** (added after the adversarial review). `ReplicatedSpace` applies `PER_ENTRY` to a withdrawal only when every add dot's node is this replica, or a hinted member whose current stay in view has lasted maxLease plus five minutes. Any other withdrawal, under the per-entry mode, keeps the later of the two horizons.
  - `GroupRuntime.hintedWriterInViewMillis(peer)` answers how long a hinted member has been in view (from `GroupMembership.inViewForMillis`), `Long.MAX_VALUE` for this node, and -1 for a writer out of view or unhinted. `GroupMembership.joinedAtMillis(peer)` tells one stay from the next.
  - The space converts the stay's start to its own clock once, at the first judgement of the stay, and keeps it. So the sweep, the door and the expiry index reckon the writer's wait on the one clock they read. `ExpiryIndexPropertyTest`, whose replica reads a space clock that steps away from its node's clock, caught a first version that mixed the two clocks.
  - The index files a withdrawal whose writer is in view, but not yet long enough, at the end of the writer's wait if that comes first. It notes a withdrawal whose writer is out of view under that writer, and files those again when the writer comes back. Each judgement looks once at each absent writer, never at every tombstone.
  - A disengagement from `PER_ENTRY` files every entry afresh, as a settlement does. Step 5b added it because below 2.5 minutes of maxLease the legacy horizon came first; with the drift floor it never does, and the refile only spares the sweep early visits. `HorizonModeTest` shows a newcomer's withdrawal kept past `L + 5 min` and collected once the newcomer has been in view 35 minutes, long before the legacy `L + 60 min`.
- **Hysteresis (RE-Q-REL-09).** `ReplicatedSpace.HorizonMode` moves through `LEGACY`, `WAITING`, `SETTLING` and `PER_ENTRY`.
  - It disengages at once when the view holds an unhinted member. The sweep and the door each check the view live, every time they judge.
  - It engages (`SETTLING`) after `horizonEngageRounds` rounds (default 3, from 1 to 64, settable at runtime). A round is one gossip period of the group, on the space's clock. Any judgement that finds an unhinted member resets the count.
  - **An addition to the design: the settle.** Once engaged, the rule comes into force one maximum lease plus five minutes later. Until then the legacy rule applies. It covers a member whose card lacked the hint while it was in view, such as a node that restarts with the hint under the same peer id. Every copy it renewed while unhinted lapses within one maximum lease, and is past its own lapse horizon five minutes later. A writer that left the view is no longer covered by the settle: the writer's half of the precondition keeps its withdrawals on the legacy rule. The step 5b record said the settle covered such a writer; that held only for copies written before it left, and the review showed the gap.
  - The cost is a delay of one maximum lease after each engagement (up to 24 hours plus five minutes in a space that saw a day-long lease). The mode then stays in force until an unhinted member appears.
- **What the network adds (found while writing P38).** Every receiver drops a frame older than five minutes (`MAX_FRAME_AGE_MILLIS`). Between two members on `wire.ae=2`, a present entry whose lease has lapsed is out of the audited set and is never offered. So a re-offer of a present copy after `L + 5 min` comes only from three sources:
  - a member on the text form, which still lists a present entry whose lease has lapsed;
  - a lagging clock within five minutes;
  - a delay below the frame age.

  The P38 probes use the first two together.

  Since the drift floor the collector waits until `L + 10 min`, and a present copy is held only by a replica whose clock still reads under `L + 5 min`, more than five minutes behind. A frame carries its sender's hybrid logical clock, which follows the newest stamp the sender has heard. A lagging replica cut off alone falls back to its own clock, so its frames read more than five minutes old at the collector and are dropped: a two-member group never carries the copy back. It is heard again only while it hears a member nearer the collector's time. The P38 probes build that case: the actor a; a bridge b four minutes behind a; and the replica c, four minutes behind while the group forms, which drifts to eight minutes behind (its clock running at half speed, never back) while a partition cuts a off from both b and c. b and c stay together, so c's stamps follow b's; b drops its lapsed copy at `L + 5 min` by its own clock, before a collects, and c still holds its copy when the partition heals, offers it, and a's door refuses it. The first version of the probe cut c off from b too, so in some runs c learned the withdrawal from b after the heal and held only the withdrawn state, and a's count of refused re-offers did not move within the window (4 failures in 6 runs; not fully traced, since the shape was not kept).
- **P40 on the real mode.** Node a writes with a 2-minute lease. Node b holds the same identity and renews to 20 minutes, and a never hears of it. Then a cancels.
  - Under `PER_ENTRY`, a collects the tombstone at `L + 10 min` and takes b's live copy back, whatever maxLease a has seen.
  - Under the legacy rule, if a has seen a 30-minute lease, it keeps the tombstone an hour, and b's copy merges into it as withdrawn. The legacy rule is safe here.
  - Under the legacy rule, if a never saw a lease as long as 20 minutes (here 2 minutes), it collects at `L + max(2 x 2 min, MAX_DRIFT)`, ten minutes, and takes the copy back too. The test advances 13 minutes, past both.
  - So the legacy rule is safe against this break whenever the judge's observed maxLease covers the other node's renewal, and the per-entry rule is not. The shorter horizon widens the exposure. That is why the precondition matters. The step 5b record said the break came from the two writers and not from the shorter horizon; the review showed that overclaimed.
  - Nothing on the wire can tell two nodes renewing one identity apart from one. The guard is the hint's documented precondition: a node that renews for an identity another node renews for at the same time sets `agentspaces.space.horizon=legacy`.
  - That precondition is stated on `PeerNode.HORIZON_HINT`, on `PeerNode.Builder.horizon`, on the property, and in SPEC §7.3.
- **Signals.** `horizonMode()`, `horizonEngagements()`, `horizonSettlements()` and `horizonDisengagements()` on `ReplicatedSpace`. The first disengagement per space logs at INFO, later ones at DEBUG.
- **Tests.** `HorizonModeTest` (P41, and the newcomer writer), `HorizonSimulationTest` on the real mode (P40 in both modes, with and without a 30-minute lease seen), `HorizonModelCheckTest` tied to the real forms, `AdversaryHorizonViewScopeTest` (a writer out of view), and the `HorizonLaggingCopyTest` probes (P38) in content, pdt, agent, store and connect-core.
